mentl/1bab9e9:
The stamp's pricing measurement ran and did two things: it killed the simple
branch and it measured the blocker on the narrow one.

Deleting the credit is refuted. With the clearing conjunct disabled, a probe
m2 built and then refused the wheel — m3 exit 1, pm3.wat zero bytes, one
diagnostic: `effect GraphRead reaches the executable root with no absorbing
handler ... Install one over the performing chain: ~> graph_handler`. The
comment's defence is exercised, once, by the wheel itself. One effect, named,
rather than an argument about dynamic installs in general.

The narrow branch cannot be written at this gate. A drained demand is a bare
NAME: demands_to_enames does env_lookup(d) and decides strictness from the
op's own EffectOpScheme plus handler_stateful(default_handler). No span, no
position, no origin reaches the gate, so it cannot tell an init's perform
from a body's — exactly the distinction the narrow fix needs. The demands
come from walk_lemit(lowered) + drain_effect_census(), so the change is at
the census, not the gate: a demand would have to carry where it was
performed.

Which makes this split smaller than band A's rather than equal to it. The
comment defends a genuinely undecidable case, a dead extent versus live
dynamic coverage. A state init is not that: it provably runs before any
install of its own handler, for every install, statically. So a census-level
origin is sound where the general extent question is not, and that is the
design the next step owes — priced as a representation change to the demand
rather than a conjunct at the gate.

build is deleted.

two-top/1bec420:
The APK build failed on main. cargo-apk panics outright when
version_name or version_code appear in [package.metadata.android] --
"version_name should not be set in TOML", cargo-apk 0.10.0 apk.rs:83 --
because it DERIVES both from the crate version:
VersionCode::from_semver(pkg.version).to_code(1). I put them in its
table. The build died in under a second, before a line was compiled.

Nothing local caught it. fmt, clippy, 602 tests and cargo metadata all
passed while the release build was broken, because no local gate touches
the Android manifest and apk.yml only runs on push to main -- so the
release build is the first thing to exercise it. That gap is worth
closing separately; a manifest error should not first surface as a
failed public release.

The goal stands: an explicit monotonic versionCode so Android's
downgrade protection engages, instead of every build carrying the same
default and letting an older APK reinstall over a newer one, keep /data,
and write profile.json back through a struct predating signing_key. The
lever is just somewhere else. [workspace.package] version 0.0.0 ->
0.15.0, which cargo-apk reads for both fields; the android table now
carries only a comment saying why it must stay empty. Tracks the sim
generation, so 0.15.0 ships SIM_VERSION 15.

Cargo.lock regenerated for the new workspace version and --locked
verified, since CI enforces it everywhere and would otherwise fail on
the lockfile rather than on anything real.

Verified on a clean target/ (the previous run hit ENOSPC mid-suite and
was discarded rather than read): cargo test --workspace --locked
--no-fail-fast 602 passed 0 failed, cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets --locked -D warnings, cargo fmt --all --check.

clob/1be39d7:
The recurrent core is a driven dynamical system, and its regime --
contractive, near-critical, expansive -- decides how long the past can
matter at all. Until now that regime was an accident of init. This
makes it a measured quantity, the way Phase A made J/nat one.

New pieces:
- State-space API: SelectiveSSM::set_state, MLGRU::set_state,
  Block::{state_dim,export_state,import_state}, and the same trio on
  CoreModel. The flat state vector is the model's entire memory of the
  past; a roundtrip test proves the snapshot is complete by demanding
  bit-identical logits on replay. BPTT window detachment (Path B
  Phase 3) needs exactly this API.
- src/dynamics/lyapunov.rs: Benettin twin-trajectory estimator for the
  largest Lyapunov exponent, generic over a TwinSystem trait and
  verified against maps with known exponents (uniform contraction ->
  ln 0.5, non-dyadic expanding sawtooth -> ln 1.9, rigid rotation -> 0,
  total collapse stays finite).
- src/dynamics/mod.rs: ModelTwin drives two copies of one model in
  lockstep through a token stream; RegimeReport serializes the verdict.
- clob regime: loads a model twice, warms up, perturbs by eps, and
  reports lambda1 in nats/token plus the e-folding memory horizon.
  TOML report with manifest sidecar.

First measurement, small config at random init on the smoke corpus:
lambda1 = -1.23 nats/token (stable across eps 1e-3..1e-5 and seeds),
memory horizon 0.8 tokens. That is the reservoir probe's zero
contextual gain explained mechanically: the frozen random core erases
a state perturbation in under one token, so no linear readout could
ever have recovered context from it. The probe said the reservoir was
dead; this instrument says why, and gives Path B a dial to watch while
the core trains.
noodles/1bcf1a3:
harmonyRate: 2 broke the painter's premise that every slot is its own
measure: eight half-bar slots engraved as eight whole-note bars, and a
borrowed A-flat beside the diatonic vi in one measure left an unmarked A
that a reader applying the measure rule hears flat. The staff was showing
one thing while playback played another.

paintChordStaff takes the rate now and draws the notation that says so:
barlines through both staves at every measure boundary, a 4/4 after the
signature, half-note stems on rate-2 towers (direction per staff by the
middle-line rule, seconds displaced to the stem's far side), and an
end-repeat at the right edge, where the wrap stubs already pointed. Both
painters track accidental state through the measure - an accidental holds
its staff position until cancelled, the cancelling natural prints, and a
re-sharpened note restates. Roll staffs sort note stacks bottom-up,
displace seconds, stagger accidental columns, and extend ledgers under
displaced heads.

Accidentals are drawn Path2D geometry now, key signatures included, with
real double-sharp and double-flat shapes guarded - the same
determinism-over-luck call as the clefs, and for the same reason: text
glyphs vary per platform and sit next to engraved outlines looking like
UI. Thin strokes clamp to a CSS pixel; 0.09 staff spaces at roll scale is
0.66 px, which is how the first draft's natural rendered as a box with
antennae.

Verified: smoke green; .tmp/pa-staff-receipts.mjs renders five plates
(rate 1, rate 2 with the cancelling-natural measure, F-sharp major's six
sharps with E-sharp engraving bare, A-flat major, extensions with a slash
bass) and three live editor shots. DESIGN-STAFF.md carries the corrected
argument in place of the retired one.

The hosted job has never executed. Six runs across three commits on main
and three on this branch all end one to three seconds after they are
created, with no logs to download, and the workflow's own usage record
reports zero billable milliseconds against a job that reports as started
and completed. Zero billable time is the tell: the job is refused at
dispatch and never reaches a runner. The workflow is state active, the
file is valid ASCII, the repository is public so minutes are not the
constraint, and the previous commit proved the earlier suspect innocent
by removing every third-party action and failing identically. Nothing in
this tree can fix it; the block is on the account.

So the laws stop depending on it. .githooks/pre-commit runs check.sh and
refuses the commit when they do not hold, naming the rebuild command
when the failure is drift, installed once per clone with
core.hooksPath and skippable with --no-verify. Verified by staging a
hand-edit of a generated file: the commit was refused and the drift
named. This is the copy that matters, because it runs where the work
happens and no hosting account can switch it off.

hand from the Actions tab the moment the account is unblocked, without
waiting for a push to prove it.
